title: isSuperAdmin() short-circuits requirePermission() regardless of held permissions
description: requirePermission.js's isSuperAdmin(req) returns true when req.isAdminPortal===true OR any req.userRoles entry has systemRoleKey==='SUPERADMIN'. When true, requirePermission/requireAnyPermission/requireAllPermissions all call next() before ever inspecting req.permissions.
steps: Construct a mock req with userRoles=[{systemRoleKey:'SUPERADMIN'}] and permissions=new Set()
Invoke requirePermission('organization.delete')(req, res, next)
expectedResult: next() is called with no arguments; res.status/json are never invoked, even though req.permissions does not contain 'organization.delete'.

title: requirePermission() returns 403 with exact message shape and logs authz.permission.denied
description: vibrantix-backend/src/middleware/requirePermission.js:25-47. On denial the middleware must return {success:false, message:'Missing permission: <perm>'} with HTTP 403, and log a structured warn event (type:'security', event:'authz.permission.denied') including userId, orgId, requiredPermission, heldPermissions, resource, action.
steps: Invoke requirePermission('policy.delete')(req, res, next) with a spy logger
Inspect the res.status/json call and the logger.warn call
expectedResult: res.status(403) and res.json({success:false, message:'Missing permission: policy.delete'}) are called; next() is never called; a warn log with event 'authz.permission.denied' and requiredPermission='policy.delete' is emitted.

title: ENFORCE_PERMISSIONS=false only disables checks when NODE_ENV is not 'production'
description: requirePermission.js:12 computes ENFORCE = (NODE_ENV==='production') || (ENFORCE_PERMISSIONS!=='false') at module load. This means production ALWAYS enforces, irrespective of ENFORCE_PERMISSIONS; the bypass is only reachable outside production.
preconditions: Test harness can reset the module cache (jest.resetModules) between env combinations
steps: Set NODE_ENV='production', ENFORCE_PERMISSIONS='false'; re-require requirePermission.js; call requirePermission('x.read') on a req with no matching permission
Set NODE_ENV='development', ENFORCE_PERMISSIONS='false'; re-require requirePermission.js; repeat the same call
Set NODE_ENV='development', ENFORCE_PERMISSIONS unset; re-require; repeat the same call
expectedResult: Case 1 (production): request is denied with 403 — ENFORCE_PERMISSIONS is ignored in production. Case 2 (development + explicit 'false'): next() is called unconditionally (bypass active). Case 3 (development, unset): request is denied with 403 (default enforcement).

title: isValidPermission() accepts catalog module.action pairs and named carve-outs, rejects everything else
description: vibrantix-backend/src/config/permissions.js:164-182. Special-cased permissions ('audit.manage', EXTRA_VALID_PERMISSIONS like 'intelli-report.publish') must validate even though they don't fit the standard MODULES x ACTIONS cross-product; nav.* must only validate against NAV_MODULES, not MODULES.
steps: Call isValidPermission('evidence.read') — expect true
Call isValidPermission('audit.manage') — expect true (special case, not in ACTIONS)
Call isValidPermission('intelli-report.publish') — expect true (EXTRA_VALID_PERMISSIONS)
Call isValidPermission('nav.evidence') — expect true; call isValidPermission('nav.organization_billing') — expect false (not a real NAV_MODULES entry)
Call isValidPermission('evidence.manage') — expect false ('manage' is not a standard ACTION for a normal module)
expectedResult: Each assertion matches the expected boolean exactly, confirming the catalog carve-outs don't accidentally widen validation for ordinary modules.

title: isOrgOnlyPermission() correctly classifies org-only vs project-scoped permission strings
description: config/permissions.js:93-101,188-191. ORG_ONLY_MODULE_PERMISSIONS explicitly whitelists only individually-verified module.action pairs (e.g. user.create, role.delete, project.create); every GRC feature module (evidence, policy, audit, risk, vendor, trust_vault, etc.) is project-scoped and must return false.
steps: Call isOrgOnlyPermission('user.create') — expect true
Call isOrgOnlyPermission('project.create') — expect true
Call isOrgOnlyPermission('project.read') — expect false (only 'create' is org-only for project; read/update/delete are membership-scoped)
Call isOrgOnlyPermission('evidence.create') — expect false (project-scoped module)
expectedResult: All four assertions match, confirming the catalog-separation source of truth has not drifted to reclassify a project-scoped module as org-only or vice versa.

title: usePermission() hook grants access via literal module wildcard string only, not derived expansion
description: vibrantix-client-panel/src/hooks/usePermission.js:33-35. The hook checks `permissions.includes(\`${permModule}.*\`)` — this only matches if the LITERAL string 'policy.*' is present in the Redux permissions array; it is not derived from any real module.action grant the user holds.
preconditions: Redux authSlice.permissions seeded per test case
steps: Render usePermission('policy.approve') with permissions=['policy.read','policy.create'] (no wildcard, no exact match) — expect false
Render usePermission('policy.approve') with permissions=['policy.*'] — expect true
Render usePermission('policy.approve') with permissions=['polic.*'] (typo'd module) — expect false
expectedResult: Only the literal 'policy.*' string unlocks every policy.* permission on the frontend; holding several individual policy permissions does not synthesize a wildcard.

title: Internal service-token comparison rejects mismatched-length tokens without throwing
description: trust-vault-service/src/routes/s2s.routes.ts:52-78, validateInternalToken(). timingSafeEqual requires equal-length Buffers; the implementation guards with a `lengthsMatch` check before calling timingSafeEqual so a shorter/longer provided token fails the comparison instead of throwing a RangeError that could crash the request handler.
steps: Call validateInternalToken() with x-internal-service-token header shorter than INTERNAL_SERVICE_TOKEN
Call validateInternalToken() with x-internal-service-token header longer than INTERNAL_SERVICE_TOKEN
Call validateInternalToken() with the exact correct token
expectedResult: Both mismatched-length calls return false / reply 401 without throwing; the exact-match call returns true. No unhandled exception in any case.

title: isProjectAdmin() grants the org-wide project bypass via either admin-portal flag or project.admin permission
description: vibrantix-backend/src/config/projectAccess.js:23-25. isProjectAdmin(req) = req.isAdminPortal===true || req.permissions.has('project.admin'). Only SUPERADMIN/ADMIN system roles (via generateFullAccess()) hold 'project.admin' — it is deliberately excluded from every project-scoped grant path.
steps: Call isProjectAdmin({isAdminPortal:true, permissions:new Set()}) — expect true
Call isProjectAdmin({isAdminPortal:false, permissions:new Set(['project.admin'])}) — expect true
Call isProjectAdmin({isAdminPortal:false, permissions:new Set(['evidence.admin'])}) — expect false
expectedResult: Only the two intended paths (admin-portal claim, project.admin permission) return true; holding an unrelated .admin permission does not.
